title: Leaner streamed-run store for clustered-key radix agg (q18 subquery)
summary:
I measured first, as the issue asked. Temporary steady_clock timers were removed before benching. They showed the cost of the streamed-run path is not mainly in the ColumnDataCollection run store. Warm CPU ms for the HAVING subquery (60M rows, 15M runs, summed over threads):
- run-head detection: ~230
- state allocation + per-row address fill: ~215
- InitializeStates: 62
- UpdateStates: 105
- CDC Append: 68
- source finalize: 88
- CDC scan: 9

Both of the top two are branchy loops over runs of ~4 rows, so most key changes mispredict. FindClusteredRuns and FindRunHeads also made two such passes over the same keys. So I fixed run detection rather than building the block store.

Change (src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp only):
- FindClusteredRuns is now one branch-free pass over the chunk's keys. It writes a candidate head at heads[n] and advances n by (cur != prev). It records the run index of every row in a lazily allocated per-thread run_ids buffer, and accumulates the "decreasing" flag without branching. There is a separate template instance with no selection vector for flat keys.
- first_end and last_start come from the head list, so the non-decreasing check and the split semantics are unchanged.
- SinkInteriorRuns reuses the chunk's heads (the interior runs are heads[1..n-2]) instead of calling FindRunHeads again; FindRunHeads is removed.
- The address fill is now a simple loop with no branches: addresses[i] = states + (run_ids[i]-1)*stride.
- When streaming is used, the run store, the states and MergeRunStores are all unchanged.

Measured:
- HAVING micro: 188-194ms → 136-143ms (~-27%).
- `SELECT DISTINCT` micro: ~140ms → 81-90ms.
- After the fix, run detection inside SinkInteriorRuns is ~1ms CPU and alloc/address fill is ~93ms.
- bench q18: -20.1%, -32.1%, -14.6%, -24.7% over four runs. q14 was -10..-15% in three runs and -2.8% in one.
- Full-bench geomean: -4.2% and -1.1%.
- Other templates are noise. q16 swung between +10% and -7.5%; its leading group key is a compressed string (UHUGEINT), so it never reaches this code. q02 and q05 were +14.5% and +9% in one run and back to -1.3% and +0.7% on recheck.

Correctness checks all matched FILTER(WHERE true) variants, which disable streaming, or the expected values:
- negative INT keys with a second group column
- UTINYINT keys
- NULL keys with HAVING
- descending (unsorted) input, which takes the fallback
- the HAVING subquery itself
- two-key group by on a filtered scan
- string_agg (destructor, so not streamed)
- count(DISTINCT)
notes:
- The issue's preferred fix (replacing the CDC run store with fixed blocks) was not done. Measurement showed CDC append plus scan is only ~77ms CPU out of ~770. An earlier session found that the block store alone gave q18 -1.4%.
- Remaining per-group CPU after this fix: alloc/address fill 93, InitializeStates 72 (an indirect call per state), UpdateStates 112, CDC append 70, FinalizeStates 90 ms. A block store with one InitializeStates per block plus arithmetic row pointers could still save ~100-150ms CPU, maybe -5% on q18, as a follow-up.
- Another earlier finding: RegisterRunInterval (mutex + std::map per chunk) costs ~69ms CPU; coalescing adjacent intervals could cut it.
- Timer method: write to a file in the worktree's gitignored tmp/ directory. stderr output makes dbe-tool fail, and reading /tmp is denied. A one-line leftover file, tmp/tmpt.txt, is still there; it is gitignored.
- q16, q02 and q05 swing ±10% between bench runs, so recheck them before trusting a single run.
